get.description:
The coordinate map derived from a resource's bytes: its recovered text plus the positioned runs that index it. Assembled via the bus gateway.

Whole-resource, not paginated — a producer iterates page by page, but every consumer wants one map: a browser quoting the text under a hand-drawn rectangle, a headless client analysing a document.

This endpoint never runs recognition. The Smelter is the sole producer and publishes at ingest; a read that finds nothing waits for that resource's content generation to settle and then answers 204. A 204 is the common case and not an error — a native text layer is read in the browser, and a media type with no extractor never produces a map at all. Callers degrade: for a PDF annotation that means geometry with no quoted text.

204.description: No map has been derived for this resource. The ordinary answer for a native text layer or a media type with no extractor — not an error, and distinct from 404, which means the resource itself is absent. Carried as an empty body rather than a JSON `null` body so that a generated client's typed 200 field stays absent: unmarshalling `null` into a struct is a no-op in several languages, which would make "no map" indistinguishable from an empty one.

put.description:
Store the coordinate map derived from a resource's bytes. The Smelter is the sole producer: it is the only process that reads those bytes at ingest, so it is the only one positioned to derive a map cheaply, and it runs separately from the backend.

Agents only. A map is derived data every consumer trusts to place annotation geometry, so a browser session must not be able to write one.

400.description: Body is not a valid AnchoredText
